title: Placement, economics and managed-compute integration
summary: RexxOS exposes current estate evidence to placement and economics while retaining separate authorities. Managed external execution is an MU control-surface extension, not a new MI or a lease authority.
invariants: Job-to-Node v0.6-network6 is the placement/admission/lease authority. The Grid may project current members and validate incarnation, but may not mint or reinterpret leases.
Cloud Economics dev8 is advisory. Its selected candidates and migration economics never grant dispatch, purchase, payment, allocation, checkpoint or data-movement authority.
Managed Compute MU dev2 must verify a genuine Job-to-Node lease and exact target generation. Colab, ZeroGPU and Windows targets are managed execution endpoints, not automatic MI estate members.
Managed Compute MU production dispatch remains disabled until durable replay/request infrastructure, atomic claim/provider idempotency and RTO2 membership-generation revalidation exist.
Queue Fabric owns durable request/reply transport, ConnectSelector owns connector choice, and RTO2 membership generation must be revalidated immediately before external effect.
procedure: Use placement-layers sphere for the current semantic admittance -> WLU -> Job-to-Node authority chain.
Feed Cloud Economics only current admissible candidate objects and preserve original object identity through advisory handoff.
Bind managed compute only after the owning MU and target generation are current; fail closed on stale membership or uncertain provider execution.
